### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activity A19 appeared in about 84 of 200 traces; among its observed outgoing transitions, roughly 46 in 100 went to A28, about 31 in 100 to A21, and about 19 in 100 to A22, with small shares of about 1 in 100 each to A14, A43 and A06 [DIR001].
- In the later window, A19 appeared in about 98 of 200 traces; transitions to A28 rose to roughly 57 in 100 and to A22 to about 27 in 100, while transitions to A21 fell to about 13 in 100; the rare edges to A14, A43 and A06 were not observed, and rare edges to A08 (about 1 in 100) and A32 (about 2 in 100) appeared [DIR001].
- The overall redirection of A19's outgoing transitions was larger than in about 99 of 100 random re-splits of the pooled data, yet it is the only item that qualified in the entire screening [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one control-flow item qualified across 82 tested units, where about 0.41 items would be expected by chance if nothing had changed — a count an unchanged process typically produces — so the apparent shift of A19's transitions away from A21 and toward A28 and A22 cannot be distinguished from sampling variation [DIR001].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

The evidence contains:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after
- Screening: 82 units tested, 1 item found, 0.41 items expected without change (control_flow family: 82 units tested, 1 item, 0.41 expected)
- One evidence item: DIR001, CF_DIR indicator on activity A19

DIR001 details:
- Source activity A19's outgoing transition distribution
- Before: A21 ~31%, A28 ~46%, A22 ~19%, A14 ~1.2%, A43 ~1.2%, A06 ~1.2%
- After: A22 ~27%, A28 ~57%, A32 ~2%, A21 ~13%, A08 ~1%
- Changes: A21 dropped from ~31% to ~13% (about -18 percentage points), A28 rose from ~46% to ~57% (+11 pp), A22 rose from ~19% to ~27% (+7 pp), A14/A43/A06 disappeared (each ~1%), A08/A32 appeared (~1-2%)
- observed_change: 0.061 (cosine dissimilarity)
- empirical_strength: 0.995 (99.5% of reference comparisons had smaller difference) — this is high, unusual for random splits
- support: 84 traces before (containing A19), 98 traces after

Judging support:
- Screening comparison: 1 item found vs 0.41 expected without change. Per the instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

So with 1 item when 0.41 are expected, this is exactly the "one or two items when fewer than one is expected" case. The instruction is explicit: choose "Insufficient evidence", however large or unusual a single item looks.

Even though empirical_strength is 0.995 (high), the screening comparison dictates insufficient evidence. The count (1) is the same order as the expectation (0.41).

So the answer: Support level: Insufficient evidence.

Observed differences section:
- Describe the DIR001 finding: In the earlier window, when A19 occurred (in about 84 of 200 traces), its outgoing transitions went mostly to A28 (~46 in 100 observed transitions) and A21 (~31 in 100), with A22 (~19 in 100) and small shares to A14, A43, A06. In the later window (A19 in about 98 of 200 traces), transitions to A28 rose to ~57 in 100 and A22 to ~27 in 100, while transitions to A21 fell to ~13 in 100; the rare edges to A14, A43, A06 were not observed, and rare edges to A08 and A32 appeared.
- Note the difference is unusual for random re-splits (empirical strength ~99.5 in 100), but a single item.

Inference:
- Support level: Insufficient evidence
- "The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process." Plus one short sentence on limitation: one control-flow item when about 0.41 would be expected by chance is what a stable process typically produces; the shift in A19's routing (A21 down, A28/A22 up) remains a hypothesis that a single indicator cannot establish.

- After: A19 present in 98/200 traces (~half). A28 ~57%, A22 ~27%, A21 ~13%, A32 ~2%, A08 ~1%.

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. One sentence limitation: "A single control-flow item (about 0.41 expected by chance across 82 units) is what a stable process typically produces, so the apparent shift of A19's transitions away from A21 and toward A28 and A22 cannot be distinguished from sampling variation [DIR001]."

That works. Check bracket rule: each bullet/paragraph ends with exactly one bracket pair. The first line "Support level: Insufficient evidence" — is that a paragraph stating a fact? It's the required first line; I won't bracket it (the examples in instructions show it without brackets). The instruction says the first line is exactly that string, so no bracket.

Also check: "Do not discuss time or resources when the evidence contains no such items." — correct, only control flow here.

Also note DIR shares caveat: shares are over observed outgoing transitions, not cases. I mentioned "among its observed outgoing transitions". Good.

Also the caveat about unobserved edges: I said "were not observed" rather than "disappeared". Good.

Length: concise. Done.
